normalized.title: TWELFTH FIXED CALL FOR PROPOSALS UNDER THE PLAN FOR EUROPEAN COOPERATING STATES (PECS) IN BULGARIA
normalized.description: The European Space Agency and the Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation of the Republic of Bulgaria hereby invite you to submit a proposal for the above Call for Proposals, which will be soon published in esa-star. While it is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, this CfP will be addressed only to Bulgarian legal entities registered in ESA-STAR, as prime tenderer and foresees the following standard activity types: Type A Research and Preparatory Activities, aimed at the preparation for participation in ESA optional programmes or the initial steps of a product development for Space, with potential for use on future ESA missions or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 1 and the target TRL shall be TRL3 or below. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. Type B Flight- and Ground Segment-related Research and Development Activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 3 and the target TRL shall be TRL 6. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 500,000 (hardware development)/EUR 250,000 (all other activities). Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000.Type E: Phase 0/A/B1 small sat mission definition studies with potential to lead to either a national or a commercial mission, in the area of Earth Observation for Climate, Agriculture, Disaster Management and Environmental Monitoring, enabling the development and demonstration of Bulgarian technologies and products in space. Maximum price for ESA 300.000 Euros. Type F Space Applications, products and services making use of ESA/ European space infrastructure that is already existing or scheduled for operation in the near term. The start TRL shall be at least 6 and the target TRL shall be TRL 8. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity. Type G1 University courses/modules leading to a qualification (BSc or MSc) in space related topics that correspond to the needs of national space industry and to encourage career in space and answer to national space industry needs. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 70,000. To be published as a separate tender in esa-star: Type G2 PhD Theses that correspond to a clear need from the national space industry and would lead to a new product or service being able to be developed. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000 with a minimum company co-funding of EUR 10,000. More information and further programmatic constraints can be consulted in the cover letter of the call upon its issue date.

normalized.title: STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSAL FOR GSTP ELEMENT 2: MAKE ACTIVITIES
normalized.description: The activities in GSTP Element 2 "Make" aim to strengthen worldwide competitiveness in the near term in existing markets, establish strategic capabilities which will result in stronger competitiveness in the medium term on existing or new markets, and to support the implementation of National priorities. GSTP Element 2 "Make" aims to support design, development, and demonstration activities. Products and technologies are defined to be any hardware, software, or applications within the scope set out in section 3 below. Key characteristics of this Element are:  The role of industry in defining and proposing projects oriented to commercial or institutional opportunities in all areas of satellite applications except satellite telecommunication (not covered by GSTP);  The outcome of an activity will eventually become a product ready for exploitation.  The sharing of funding by ESA and industry. Activities submitted in the frame of GSTP Element 2 Make" may be related to the improvement or development of satellite subsystems or equipment (including EGSE), space transportation subsystems or equipment up to engineering model or qualification model, and the improvement or development of ground / user system and equipment up to prototypes and commercialized products. Activities should address any the following technology themes: Earth observation, science, exploration, human spaceflight, space transportation, satellite navigation or generic technologies.

normalized.title: CALL FOR PROPOSALS FOR DOWNSTREAM APPLICATIONS IN ARTES 4.0 (UNDER BASS, 4S OR 5G PROGRAMME LINES)FEASIBILITY STUDIES/DEMONSTRATION PROJECTS
normalized.description: The overall goal of ARTES 4.0 Business Applications can be summarised as the development of pre-operational services - possibly in partnership - for a wide range of users through the combination of different systems. Business Applications activities aim at: i) collecting user feedback for better tuning of the applications and the operation of all elements involved, ii) developing commercial sustainable space based applications by linking user needs to corresponding solutions incorporating space assets requesting only limited technology adaptations, iii) demonstrating to users and stakeholders that the proposed solutions work in their operational environment and are compatible with their operational practices, iv) utilising at least one space asset (such as Satellite Communications, Earth Observation, Satellite Navigation, Human Spaceflight, or any other space asset, service or technology), leading to a better exploitation of existing space capacity and know-how together with a better understanding of how they should evolve to respond to user needs. ARTES 4.0 Business Applications operates via a 'Call for Proposals' which is always open. Partners respond with proposals as they find it opportune. The activities proposed in response to this 'Call for Proposals' must be relevant to above mentioned ARTES 4.0 Business Applications objectives. normalized.title: INCUBED CALL FOR PROPOSAL: STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSALS
normalized.description: The InCubed Element of the European Earth Watch Programme (InCubed) aims to accompany European economic operators in the rapid evolution of the Earth Observation market, both in Europe and globally. InCubed introduces a dedicated process within ESA Earth Observation programmes to strengthen and stimulate the development of near-to-market commercial initiatives in partnership with industry. Activities supported under InCubed include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (e.g. missions, instruments, prototype elements of EO constellations), innovative mission management solutions (including for future EO constellations), as well as the development of ground, data, and application platforms. InCubed targets commercial viability by the end of the activity (at least at minimum viable product level) and requires a substantial degree of innovation, i.e. the creation of new value within the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement is mandatory, with customers acting as beta testers and validators of the developed product or service. Customer engagement must be clearly demonstrated at both pitch and proposal stages, and letters of support or interest from potential customers are considered a strong asset. The scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves, in line with the objectives of InCubed. Two development cycles are available within InCubed, depending on the maturity of the concept: De-risking Cycle (typically starting from TRL 4), focusing on reducing technical and market risks;Product Development Cycle (typically starting from TRL 6), aiming at delivering a product ready for commercialisation. Under this Call for Proposals, economic operators are invited to submit their ideas via the OSIP (Open Space Innovation Platform) (ideas.esa.int), which serves as the entry point for the programme. The application process consists of the following step: Idea Pitch - Applicantssubmit and present a draft Outline proposal via OSIP to ESA (and potentially the relevant National Delegation(s)). Following a positive assessment, economic operators will be invited to submit a Proposal Part 2 (Full) in accordance with the established procedures and evaluation criteria. Activities supported under InCubed are based on a co-funding scheme, whereby economic operators contribute financially to the project, demonstrating commitment to and confidence in their business case.

normalized.title: INCUBED-2 STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSAL
normalized.description: The InCubed Element of the European Earth Watch Programme (InCubed) aims at accompanying the European economic operators in the Earth Observation market rapid evolution currently witnessed in Europe and overseas. InCubed offers a new process in ESA Earth Observation programmes to strengthen and stimulate the realization of endeavours near-to-the-market with Economic Operators. Activities to be supported include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (missions, instruments, prototype element of EO constellation), innovative mission management solution, including for future EO constellation, the development of application platforms, etc. InCubed is looking for commercial viability by the end of the activity (up to at least a minimum viable product level) and a substantial degree of innovation i.e. adding new value to the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement/involvement is mandatory. Commercial customers are encouraged to be either as part of the consortium representing the value chain or as beta testers/validators of the developed product/service.  Customer engagement/involvement must be highlighted at the pitch and proposal stage. Letters of potential customer support/interest are seen as a very positive aspect. The actual scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves in relevance to the InCubed objectives. Two development cycles are possible within InCubed: TheDe-Risking Cycle (start TRL 4) and Product Development Cycle (startTRL 6) depending on the maturity of the concept being developed. Regarding this forthcoming Announcement of Partnership Opportunity, Economic operators are invited to register and submit idea pitches onto ideas.esa.int (InCubed channel). Following a positive pitch meeting, the second step is to fill in a Part 1 (Outline) proposal template, which must be supported by the Participating State(s) having jurisdiction over them. Following a positive assessment,the economic operators will be invited to submit a Part 2 (Full) proposal template, as per established procedure and evaluation criteria. The proposals to be supported by InCubed will have to be co-funded by the economic operators (partnership agreements), as a sign of their engagement and belief in their own business case.

normalized.title: NAVIGATION INNOVATION SUPPORT PROGRAMME ELEMENT 3 STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSALS
normalized.description: Under NAVISP Element 3, the Agency issues this Call for Proposals for the development of initiatives in the Position, Navigation and Timing domain. Element 3 is focused on participating States' priorities and aims at supporting their national navigation activities along the whole value chain. Element 3 configures as an ad-hoc support element, which is envisaged per country and possibly per domain, for the development and promotion of products, applications and services based on GNSS and more widely on PNT systems. Following participating states request, ESA may provide technical assistance in various areas. Element 3 configures as an opportunity for the participating States delegations to animate and coordinate discussions with national entities and to set up the processes to identify and federate institutional demands. This will foster cooperation as well as possible national partnerships with a wide diversity of actors, enlarging the national space community (agency, industries, universities, and research centres) and strengthening its relationships with authorities, organisations, institutions, industries, and research actors from non-space sectors. Industry and research institutes of Participant States are encouraged to contact the NAVISP Element 3 team to discuss the development of activities of national relevance and matching institutional interests. Details on the tendering process and preparing the Full Proposal are provided in the Standard Call for Proposals.

normalized.title: SECOND STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSALS FOR LUXIMPULSE PROGRAMME ACTIVITIES
normalized.description: The Luxembourg's National Programme - LuxIMPULSE Programme, aims to strengthen worldwide competitiveness of Luxembourg industry in the near term in existing markets and to establish strategic capabilities which will result in stronger competitiveness in the medium term on existing or new markets, and to support the implementation of Luxembourg national priorities.The Call for Proposals is addressed only to economic operators - be it as Prime or Subcontractor level - registered in Luxembourg, unless otherwise instructed and approved by the Luxembourg Space Agency. The proposed work shall not overlap with any currently running ESA Contract awarded to any entity in the proposal consortium.Activities submitted in the frame of LuxIMPULSE Programme may be related to the study, improvement or development of space systems, subsystems, technology, ground systems for space applications, or downstream service products based on space data.It must be noted that according to the Procurement Regulations ESA/REG/001 rev. 5, Art. 18, Tenderers areeligible to participate in a tendering procedure of the Agency provided they possess the necessary professional and technical qualifications, professional and technical competences, financial resources, equipment and other physical facilities, managerial capability, reliability, experience and the personnel, to perform a Contract.The support to the activity by the Luxembourg Space Agency is mandatory. The activities selected will be funded by the Agency at a level depending on the nature of the economic operator and the maturity and proximity to market of the activity. The remainder will be funded by the economic operator's internal own resources and shall not include any additional source of public funding. The economic operator's contribution can be either monetary or in-kind.

The TTC services aim at the reception of the satellite telecommands, their modulation and radiation to the satellite.Although covering different functions of the Copernicus Space Component (CSC) operations, the above-mentioned services may be considered rather similar in terms of required infrastructure and operations capabilities of the service providers. Accordingly the current procurement will include the possibility to cover both services.Building upon the operational experience gathered in the past years since the launch of Sentinel-1A in 2014, ESA intends to procure as much as possible standardized services using Contractors' owned state-of-the-art, off-the-shelf facilities and satellite-independent interfaces.In order to maximize the competition and the value for money for the to-be-procured services, the Services will be procured through the ESA Framework Agreements procedure, as established at Article 15 of ESA Procurement Regulations (ESA/REG/001, rev. 3 which can be downloaded at the following URL http://emits.sso.esa.int/emits/owa/emits.main). Pozostałe wymagania dotyczące przedmiotu zamówienia oraz obowiązki wykonawcy wskazano we wzorze umowy, stanowiącym Część III SWZ. 5. Wykonawca jest zobowiązany do udzielenia zamawiającemu gwarancji jakości i zobowiązany jest do wykonywania świadczeń z niej wynikających. Wymagania dotyczące gwarancji zostały określone w Części III i IV SWZ. 6. Dostarczony przedmiot zamówienia musi być fabrycznie nowy, nieeksponowany na wystawach, kompletny i sprawny technicznie. Przez stwierdzenie „fabrycznie nowy” należy rozumieć przedmiot zamówienia oryginalnie zapakowany, nieużywany przed dniem dostarczenia, z wyłączeniem używania niezbędnego dla przeprowadzenia testu jego poprawnej pracy po wyprodukowaniu. 7. Dostarczony przedmiot zamówienia musi być wolny od jakichkolwiek wad fizycznych i prawnych oraz roszczeń osób trzecich. 8. Dostarczony przedmiot zamówienia musi pochodzić z kanału dystrybucyjnego producenta niewyłączającego dystrybucji na rynek polski i zapewniającego realizację uprawnień gwarancyjnych. 9. Przedmiot zamówienia musi być dostarczony wraz z instrukcjami obsługi, sterownikami oraz ewentualnym oprogramowaniem towarzyszącym niezbędnym do prawidłowego korzystania z przedmiotu zamówienia (uzyskania pełnej funkcjonalności wskazanej w Części IV SWZ). Zamawiający nie będzie zobowiązany do wnoszenia żadnych dodatkowych należności, w szczególności opłat licencyjnych, zaś ewentualne licencje będą udzielone w ramach wynagrodzenia wykonawcy, bez ograniczenia czasowego i terytorialnego, chyba że w Części IV SWZ wyraźnie zaznaczono inaczej. Jeżeli do uruchomienia i korzystania z tego oprogramowania potrzebne będą licencje, kody lub inne uprawnienia muszą być one dostarczone bez dodatkowych opłat. Kody, licencje i inne uprawnienia muszą być dostarczone również wówczas, gdy są niezbędne do uruchomienia albo skonfigurowania elementów sprzętowych. Instrukcje obsługi, sterowniki i ewentualne oprogramowanie towarzyszące należy dostarczyć w momencie przekazania dokumentacji powykonawczej. Wymóg, o którym mowa w zdaniu pierwszym wykonawca może spełnić poprzez zapewnienie zamawiającemu dostępu do serwisu internetowego producenta, na którym dostępne będą instrukcje, oprogramowanie w języku polskim lub angielskim itd. W takim wypadku wykonawca zobowiązany jest przekazać zmawiającemu wraz z dokumentacją powykonawczą kody, hasła itp. o ile są niezbędne do skorzystania z tego serwisu. 10. Oferowany przedmiot zamówienia w dniu sporządzenia oferty nie może być przewidziany przez producenta do wycofania z produkcji lub sprzedaży. 11. Dostarczony przedmiot zamówienia przeznaczony do zasilania z sieci energetycznej musi być wyposażony w odpowiednią liczbę kabli zasilających pozwalających na podłączenie go do standardowych gniazdek zasilających, chyba że w Części IV SWZ zaznaczono inaczej. 12. W dacie odbioru przedmiotu zamówienia System musi być kompletny, w pełni uruchomiony i gotowy do użytkowania. Wszystkie elementy wchodzące w skład Systemu muszą być prawidłowo przygotowane, zainstalowane, skonfigurowane i wzajmenie połączone, zgodnie z wymaganiami określonymi w SWZ, dokumentacją techniczną oraz zasadami wiedzy technicznej i obowiązującymi przepisami prawa.
